title: Hybrid burst shaping and pass-through overage accounting
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers on Redwood Dedicated have unpredictable costs when short-term demand exceeds reserved throughput. Current surge pools provide temporary headroom but either (a) strictly absorb cost on customer invoice with opaque allocation, or (b) throttle requests and cause degraded SLAs. We need a mechanism that shapes bursts across a customer fleet and produces transparent pass-through overage charges that map to per-route usage while preserving latency SLOs where possible.

This ticket implements a hybrid burst-shaping controller plus a pass-through overage accounting model: the controller will softly shape incoming requests across a configurable grace window (burst_shaping_window_ms) and use proportional request admission to reduce sudden pressure on the fleet. When shaping cannot prevent capacity exceedance, the platform marks requests that consumed temporary headroom and bills them as pass-through overage using a predictable per-token rate, with invoice metadata linking usage to the route, model variant, and surge pool identifier. The design emphasizes predictable economics, operator visibility, and simple customer-facing bills rather than opaque pooled credits.

Goals:
- Preserve latency SLOs for prioritized routes using shaping and priority lanes.
- Provide clear per-route overage line-items with rate-tiering and time-limited discounts.
- Allow operators to adjust shaping aggressiveness and grace windows per-fleet.
- Keep runtime complexity low and avoid per-request heavy bookkeeping in hot paths.

Non-goals:
- Replacing long-term reserved capacity commitments or refunds models.
- Implementing auction-based burst allocation in this change (deferred to future ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Burst shaping controller deployed to staging and can be toggled by fleet
Requests that are shaped are tagged with 'shaped=true' in tracing and show up in consoles
When temporary headroom is consumed, invoice records contain a pass-through overage line referencing: route_id, model_variant, surge_pool_id, start_ts, end_ts
Billing computation for pass-through overage matches test vectors and unit-tests for rate tiers (flat, 2-tier, and time-limited discount)
No regression in median latency for non-prioritized routes in canary (<= +5ms), and P95 for prioritized routes remains within SLO
Operator UI shows current shaping pressure, per-fleet headroom consumed, and projected overage at current rate
design_notes:
Controller design overview: a lightweight frontdoor admission filter evaluates incoming request metadata (route, priority, token_estimate), consults the fleet's shaping policy (burst_shaping_window_ms, max_inflight_ratio, priority_fraction), and decides to allow, shape (delay up to T ms), or mark for overage. Shaping is implemented via a token-bucket-like reservoir per-priority with leaky replenishment matching fleet throughput profile.

Accounting path: shaped requests are not billed immediately as overage; only when the reservoir is exhausted AND immediate admission would violate the fleet's throughput guarantee we tag subsequent requests as 'overage_consumed=true'. The billing pipeline consumes these tags asynchronously, aggregating them into per-customer, per-route usage buckets every 1 minute. Aggregation output includes dimensions required for invoices.

Telemetry and tracing: add structured trace attributes (redwood.burst.shape=true/false, redwood.burst.overage=true/false, redwood.surge_pool_id=xxx) to connect runtime behavior to billing records.

Runtime performance considerations: the admission filter must run in the hot path with a single atomic read of reservoir state. Updates to reservoirs are batched back to the fleet-state store to reduce contention. The controller supports a 'fast-path' mode that bypasses shaping decisions for requests marked as internal-health-checks or infra-heartbeat routes.
billing_spec:
Billing model: pass-through overage is computed at invoice-time by multiplying overage_units by the active per-unit rate. Rate selection logic: 1) if fleet has an active discount window (discount_pct, discount_until_ts) apply discounted rate; 2) else apply tiered rate: first N tokens at rate R1, remaining at R2. Overage_units are derived from token_estimate when request is admitted as overage; in cases of streaming generation the token count is reconciled against actual tokens emitted in post-processing to correct final billing.

Invoice metadata must include: customer_id, route_id, model_variant, surge_pool_id, interval_start, interval_end, overage_units, rate_applied, prorated_factor, operator_note.

Grace refunds: if operator cancels/rolls back a surge_pool or determines a billing error within 14 days, support team can issue a pass-through credit referencing the surge_pool_id and invoice lines. Credits are applied as separate invoice lines labeled 'surge_correction'.
rollout_plan:
1) Unit tests and billing pipeline simulation (local)
2) Canary deploy: enable shaping controller for internal test tenants on a single zone and monitor latency/throughput for 48h
3) Enable pass-through tagging in billing pipeline and run a dry-run mode where invoices aren’t emitted but recorded in a shadow table for reconciliation
4) After 72h of stable metrics, enable invoicing for a small percentage (<5%) of customers with email notification and opt-out option
5) Ramp to all Dedicated fleets over 2 weeks with customer comms and updated docs
6) Post-launch audit: reconcile shadow invoices vs emitted invoices and review operator runbook updates
monitoring:
Dashboards: Shaping Pressure (reservoir utilization), Overage Rate (overage_units/min), Latency by priority lane, Surge Pool headroom remaining. Alerts: Reservoir utilization > 85% for 5m (P1 alert), Overage rate spikes > 3x baseline for 10m (P1), Billing pipeline aggregation failures (P0).

SLOs to watch: P95 latency for prioritized routes, billing aggregation lag (< 2 minutes), accuracy reconciliation (< 0.1% mismatch vs trace-captured tokens)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect token estimates causing billing disputes. Mitigation: Reconcile streaming counts post-hoc and allow credit adjustments; surface discrepancy metrics per-customer.
Risk: Admission filter adds measurable latency. Mitigation: Optimize fast-path, precompute policy lookups, and benchmark under load.
Risk: Operators misconfigure aggressive shaping causing dropped requests. Mitigation: Provide safe defaults, validation on UI, and simulated 'what-if' tool in Console.
operator_runbook:
Immediate actions: If P95 latency for prioritized routes exceeds SLO after enabling shaping, temporarily set fleet.shaping_enabled=false for that fleet and escalate. For billing disputes: run reconciliation from trace logs (filter redwood.burst.overage=true) and create surge_correction credit if mismatch > 1%.

Post-incident: capture a timeline, list of API keys affected, surge_pool_id, and run the billing dry-run reconciliation job. Notify Finance and CS within 4 hours for customer-impacting invoices.
